chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham or someone else. He said:

I once climbed the mountain of Abu Qubays while the people were praying Maghrib, and I saw that the sun had not yet set but had merely hidden behind the mountain from the people. So I met Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and informed him of that.

He said to me: And why did you do that? Woe to what you did! You should only pray it when you do not see it behind a mountain, whether it has fully set or gone down, so long as it is not covered by a cloud or a darkness that shades it. For indeed, your concern is only your own sunrise and sunset, and the people do not have to go searching.

key_terms.المغرب: Maghrib prayer, the sunset prayer, one of the five daily prayers performed after sunset
key_terms.توارت: Hidden, concealed; refers to the sun being blocked from view by an obstruction without having truly set
key_terms.مشرقك ومغربك: Your own sunrise and sunset; refers to each person's local observable horizon for determining prayer times

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about praying Maghrib when the sun is hidden behind a mountain?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a practical jurisprudential question about the timing of Maghrib prayer. Zayd al-Shahham climbed the mountain of Abu Qubays near Mecca and discovered the sun was still visible above the horizon while the people in the valley below were already praying Maghrib. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rebuked him, ruling that one should pray based on their own visible horizon rather than investigating further. This establishes the principle that prayer timing is determined by local observation, not absolute astronomical sunset.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from Hamad b. `Isa from Hariz b. `Abdullah from Abi Aslama Zayd al-Shahham or someone else. He said:

I climbed the mountain of Abi Qubays, and the people were praying Maghrib, yet I saw that the Sun had not set, but rather it was hidden behind the mountain from the people. So, I met Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as), and I informed him of that.

So, he said to me: Why did you do that? Woe to what you did. Rather, pray [even] if you do not see it [and it is] behind a mountain, whether it has [fully] set, so long that it is not covered by a cloud or darkened by a darkness. Surely, you must take to your [own] sunrise and sunset [from your own perspective]; and the people do not have to go searching.
